text:
Replays a repository's Git history as a keystroke-level animation. Each commit is typed into the file it touched in real time, with tree-sitter syntax highlighting across 29 languages and a project tree that updates as files appear, move and disappear. Where typical git visualizers show a graph or a diff, gitlogue shows the act of editing.

Works on any local repo. Pick a commit, a range, an author or a date filter, or launch with no arguments for an endless screensaver of random commits. Nine built-in themes plus a YAML override for typing speed, colors and layout.

Turns any codebase into a typing practice ground. gittype reaches into a Git repository, extracts real functions and code blocks across 20+ languages with tree-sitter, and serves them as live typing challenges with WPM, accuracy and consistency tracking. Where typing apps usually generate prose or lorem ipsum, gittype trains you on actual code: your own current directory, any GitHub repository you point it at, or a list of trending repos refreshed daily.

Multiple game modes (Normal, Time Attack, custom difficulty levels), 15+ themes, pause/resume without losing stats, and a ranking system that issues developer titles based on cumulative performance.

Serves a directory of markdown files as a live, browsable wiki at http://localhost:8521. Run `npx mdts` in any folder and you get a three-pane web UI immediately: file tree on the left, rendered markdown in the middle, table of contents on the right, with live reload as files change.

Where mkdocs or docusaurus need a config file and a build step, mdts treats whatever is on disk as the source. Glob filtering narrows scope (`-g 'docs/**/*.md'`) when you only want a subset. Common use case: reviewing the markdown an AI assistant has just generated across many files in a Claude Code or Cursor session.
